question: A farmer divides his herd of \(n\) cows among his four sons so that one son gets one-half the herd, a second son one-fourth, a third son one-fifth, and the fourth son \(7\) cows. Then \(n\) is:
solution:
All three stated fractions refer to the whole herd. Together, the first three sons receive
\[
\frac12+\frac14+\frac15
=\frac{10+5+4}{20}
=\frac{19}{20}.
\]
The fourth son therefore receives \(1-\frac{19}{20}=\frac1{20}\) of the herd. Since that share is \(7\) cows, the whole herd has
\[
n=7\div\frac1{20}=7\cdot20=140
\]
cows. The resulting shares are \(70,35,28,7\), all whole numbers totaling \(140\). The answer is \(140\), choice C.
